text:
support-alex: customer reported p99 jump on /v1/generate — says it went from ~220ms to ~2.3s around 2024-11-28T15:12Z. They attached a screenshot of our p99 panel but raw histogram doesn't show same spike. https://dash.redwood.internal/d/abc123 :frowning:
eng-sre-maya: thanks alex. do we have trace IDs or request ids? can you paste a sample request? :eyes:
support-alex: I asked for request ids, customer gave these request_ids: [r_9a1b, r_9a2c]. they also said retries happened client-side. no obvious 5xx in logs.
eng-metrics-samir: linking in — this sounds like the usual p99 vs histogram bucketization mismatch. are we sure the panel is using the same aggregation window and source as the histogram?
ops-elena: FYI I saw a small rollout yesterday for the auth proxy at 15:05 that temporarily increased tail latency for auth handshakes. Could be correlated. rollout id: rollout/2024-11-28-auth-proxy-v4
support-alex: customer says they saw increased client-side retries which would amplify observed p99 — they hit our retries after auth delay. they want root cause.
eng-sre-maya: samir, can you check whether dashboard panel uses rollup metric (rollup.latency_ms.p99) vs raw histogram (ingest.histogram.latency_ms)? sometimes rollup uses sampled rolling window and can show spikes even when histograms seem flat.
eng-metrics-samir: digging — panel query: ``SELECT quantile(0.99) FROM rollups WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND env='prod' GROUP BY 1m`` histogram query: ``histogram_bucket_stats(route='/v1/generate', window='5m')``. I also see ingestion flagged a few events as outliers around 15:12. pinging ingest-bot.
ingest-bot: noticed delayed batch flush at 2024-11-28T15:11:58 — shard-7 had a 6s stall during flush; affected ~1200 events. root cause: disk IO contention on node i-0abc.
eng-sre-maya: that explains it — rollup p99 calculation is sensitive to late-arriving high-latency samples. histograms aggregated by bucket on ingest time may diffuse the spike depending on bucket boundaries.
jonah: can you show a quick repro of how this skews p99? maybe a tiny example.
eng-metrics-samir: example: if you have latencies [100,120,130,2000] the 99th percentile over 1m is ~2000ms. but if histogram buckets are coarse (0-100,100-500,500-5000) the bucket-count method may smooth it out depending on bucket boundaries and rollup algorithm.
eng-sre-maya: mitigation options: 1) mark ingest shard as degraded and backfill corrected flushes, 2) change rollup to use arrival-time window and ignore late samples for realtime SLO dashboards, 3) add a transient note to customer's incident while we investigate.
ops-elena: I already restarted i-0abc and increased disk throughput for shard-7. backfill job queued.
support-alex: told customer we suspect delayed ingest + auth-proxy rollout overlap; offered timeline and mitigation steps. customer asked for ETA on fix and whether their billing could be adjusted due to retries.
eng-metrics-samir: for billing — token-metering uses the request-completion event which was delayed for those users, so billable tokens likely recorded correctly; but we should audit edge-case double-charges if client retried and server accepted both.
jonah: also recommend adjusting dashboard to show both raw histogram and rollup p99 side-by-side and add a tooltip explaining rollup sensitivity to late samples. small UX change but will reduce tickets.
eng-sre-maya: agree. I'll open a follow-up: FR-2371 to add side-by-side comparison and add note.
support-alex: customer accepted timeline and asked to be notified when backfill completes. I'll follow up. :thumbsup:
metrics-bot: backfill job completed for shard-7 at 2024-11-28T16:05Z. applied corrected ingest timestamps.
eng-metrics-samir: after backfill, p99 for that minute dropped back to ~240ms in rollup. pushing a note to the dashboard: "spike due to delayed ingest + auth-proxy rollout".
eng-sre-maya: closing loop: root cause = transient disk IO stall causing delayed batch flushes that created late-arriving high-latency samples which disproportionately affected rollup p99; contributing factor = auth-proxy rollout increasing auth latency and client retries. mitigations taken: restart + disk throughput increase, backfill, dashboard clarification, rollout postmortem.
support-alex: I'll update the customer thread with root cause, ETA, and note on billing audit. thanks team. :heart:
